name: Chatleadr
author: chatleadr

sections.description:
Chatleadr is an AI chatbot that answers your visitors’ questions and captures their details as leads. This plugin adds your Chatleadr bot to your WordPress site without any code.

You need a Chatleadr account to use the plugin. The free plan includes one bot and 50 conversations a month, and you can create the account from the plugin.

Features:

  • Connect in a few clicks. Create a free account from the plugin, or connect a bot you already have with a connection code or a secret key.
  • Choose where the bot appears. Show it on every public page or only on the paths you list, and keep it off paths such as /checkout.
  • Preview before you publish. Show the bot only to logged-in staff, on your real pages and theme, while visitors see nothing.
  • Follow your results. See the last seven days of conversations and leads on this site, and its recent leads, in WordPress admin.
  • No code on excluded pages. The plugin decides on your server whether a page shows the bot, so pages you exclude carry no Chatleadr code at all.

External services

This plugin connects to Chatleadr (https://chatleadr.com), the service that runs your chatbot. The plugin cannot work without it.

  • api.chatleadr.com: the plugin sends your site’s domain and your bot’s secret key to load the bot’s settings, its statistics and your account notices, and to check whether the bot is switched on. That check runs at most once a minute, when someone views a page that shows the bot. While you connect for the first time, the plugin also sends a one-time connection identifier and token, and the six-digit connection code shown on the Chatleadr screen.
  • chat.chatleadr.com: on the pages where the bot appears, your visitors’ browsers load the chat window from here. Chatleadr handles their conversations with the bot. The chat window shows a small “Powered by Chatleadr” link, which plans with white-labelling can remove.
  • app.chatleadr.com: links on the plugin’s screens open Chatleadr for sign-up and account management.

The Recent Leads tab shows the leads your bot captured on this site, including names, email addresses, phone numbers and AI-written conversation summaries. The plugin fetches them only when you open that tab and never stores them in your WordPress database. Only aggregate figures, such as conversation and lead counts, are cached, and they contain no personal data. Your page visibility rules are evaluated on your own server and are never sent to Chatleadr.

Your use of Chatleadr is covered by its Terms of Service (https://docs.chatleadr.com/legal/terms/) and Privacy Policy (https://docs.chatleadr.com/legal/privacy/). The Data Processing Terms (https://docs.chatleadr.com/legal/processing/) and the list of sub-processors (https://docs.chatleadr.com/legal/subprocessors/) are published with them.

Source code

This plugin is free software, licensed under the GPLv2 or later. The Chatleadr service it connects to is not open source and is covered by its Terms of Service.

admin/js/chatleadr-admin.bundle.js is the only minified file. It draws the chart on the plugin's screens and is built with esbuild from:
  • admin/js/chatleadr-admin.js, included in this plugin unminified.
  • Chart.js 4 (https://www.chartjs.org/), MIT licence. Source: https://github.com/chartjs/Chart.js

To rebuild it, run npm install && npm run build:js in the plugin folder. package-lock.json pins the exact versions. Every other file in the plugin is unminified source.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress admin, go to Plugins → Add Plugin, search for Chatleadr, then click Install Now and Activate. You can also upload the chatleadr folder to /wp-content/plugins/ and activate it on the Plugins screen.
  2. Open the Chatleadr menu.
  3. To start with a new Chatleadr account, click Create Free Account. The bot you create connects to this site.
  4. To connect a bot you already have, click I Already Have an Account, sign in, choose the bot, enter the Connection code this screen shows and click Connect bot. You can also connect with a secret key, as described in the first question below.
  5. On the Settings & Rules tab, under Page Visibility Rules, choose the pages the bot appears on.
sections.faq:
Where do I find my secret key?

Sign in to Chatleadr at app.chatleadr.com and open your bot’s Channels tab. Click Connect on the WordPress card, then click Create secret key. An Owner or Admin of the workspace can create the key.

Chatleadr shows the key once, so copy it before you close the window. In WordPress, paste it into Chatleadr Secret Key on the plugin’s Settings & Rules tab. If you no longer have the key, open the same card again, click Replace key and paste the new key into the plugin. The old key stops working at once.

Do I need a Chatleadr account?

Yes. The plugin adds your Chatleadr bot to your site, and the bot runs on Chatleadr. The free plan includes one bot and 50 conversations a month, and paid plans add more.

Can I try the bot before my visitors see it?

Yes. On the Settings & Rules tab, under Page Visibility Rules, turn off Publish on all public pages and turn on Preview mode. The bot then appears only to logged-in users who can edit posts, such as administrators, editors and authors. Visitors see nothing. Your Included Paths and Excluded Paths still apply, so you see what your visitors will get.

Use this to approve a bot someone else built for you on your own pages before your visitors see it. You do not need a Chatleadr login to use preview. Chatleadr labels the conversations you start in preview as test chats, so you can tell them apart from your visitors’ conversations.

Does the plugin slow down my site?

The plugin decides on your server whether a page shows the bot, so pages it is excluded from carry no Chatleadr code. Where the bot does appear, the chat window loads from Chatleadr without blocking your page. At most once a minute, the plugin also checks with Chatleadr whether your bot is switched on, which adds one short request to a single page view.

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes. A page cache stores each page as it was when cached, with or without the bot. After you switch the bot on or off in Chatleadr, or change your page visibility rules, clear your page cache so that visitors see the change.
sections.changelog:
1.1.7

  • The Settings & Rules tab shows the Authentication heading once. It used to appear twice.

1.1.6

  • The Chatleadr menu now sits below Settings, after the WordPress menus, and the Chatleadr Dashboard widget no longer moves itself to the top of your Dashboard.
  • Account notices on other admin screens are limited to warnings and errors, such as a failed payment. Every notice still shows on the Chatleadr screen and the Dashboard.
  • A new Disconnect button removes this site’s secret key, so you can connect another bot or create a new account. It is on the Settings & Rules tab and on the Connection Issue message.
  • If Chatleadr stops accepting this site’s secret key, for example because it was replaced or the bot was archived, the Chatleadr screen now says the site was disconnected.
  • If Chatleadr ends a connection before it completes, for example after five wrong connection codes, the waiting screen now says so at once. It used to wait 15 minutes.
  • Every message on the plugin’s screens can now be translated.

1.1.5

  • The Chatleadr screen shows the current Chatleadr logo.
  • A new I Already Have an Account button connects a bot you already have. Chatleadr opens on its sign-in page instead of signup, then asks for the connection code this screen shows.
  • If your browser blocks the tab that Create Free Account opens, the plugin now says so and moves on to the waiting screen, where Reopen Onboarding Tab opens it. It used to do nothing.

1.1.4

  • Chatleadr now labels the conversations you start in Preview mode as test chats, so you can tell them apart from your visitors’ conversations.
  • Overview and Recent Leads now show this site’s conversations and leads only. Leads from WhatsApp, Instagram or another website stay on the Leads page in Chatleadr.

1.1.3

  • Clearer wording on the plugin’s screens and in its error messages. The description under Publish on all public pages now says correctly that turning it off hides the bot from every visitor.

1.1.2

  • The plugin is now published by Chatleadr.

1.1.1

  • When you switch your bot on or off in Chatleadr, your site follows within two minutes. Before, the site kept the old setting until someone opened the Chatleadr screen in WordPress admin.

1.1.0

  • While the plugin waits to connect, the Chatleadr screen shows a six-digit connection code. If you already have a Chatleadr account, sign in, choose the bot for this site and enter the code to connect it.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release.
